Distilling complexity
into clarity.

Modern brand identities struggle to keep up with content demands, leading to fragmented systems, weaker messaging and declining loyalty. My approach builds brands as evolving ecosystems—identities that adapt to context, grow with knowledge and move with culture.Most identities today cannot keep pace with the volume of output modern brands demand. The result is always the same: design systems fracture, messages dilute and the loyalty that took years to build quietly erodes. Over the course of my practice, I have developed a way of building brands that function as living ecosystems rather than fixed objects. An identity, like a human one, should evolve with knowledge, adapt to context and move with culture. That is what I build.

I’m a brand designer based in Salzburg. At LOOP, I develop visual systems and shape the concepts behind pitches: finding the visual way into a brand and the idea that lets it scale. Before that, I spent two years at Studio Herrström working on identities and campaigns for Spotify, Meta, Sony Music and Red Bull Music, as well as work for Alto New York that won multiple awards, including Cannes Lions. Alongside this, I take on the occasional independent project.

Clarity fuels
transformation.

A strong result depends on its foundation. Every project follows a four-step process, starting with understanding competition, culture and audience behavior before any design decisions. This groundwork separates design that simply looks good from design that performs.The output is only as good as what leads to it. Every project follows the same four-step process. Most brand problems are not design problems. They are clarity problems. Before a single visual decision is made, I invest time understanding the competitive context, the culture and the audience’s actual behavior. This groundwork is what separates work that looks good from work that performs.

01 Research
+

Understanding is built through research and collaboration. We define what is truly needed and why it matters by aligning with stakeholders, analyzing competitors and studying the audience—creating a shared foundation for all decisions.Understanding is created, not assumed. Through careful research and open collaboration, I define what the brand needs and why it matters, before design takes form. This includes stakeholder interviews, competitive landscape mapping and audience analysis. The output is a shared understanding that guides every decision that follows.

Workshop · Competitive analysis · Audience analysis
02 Construct
+

From these insights, I define what makes the brand distinct: its positioning, its messaging and a clear brand architecture that stays consistent while remaining adaptable.Based on the findings, I build the strategic core of the brand: positioning, messaging and a clear brand architecture, derived from what makes it distinct. Strategy is only useful if it can be acted on, so it has to be specific enough to be consistent and open enough to evolve.

Positioning · Brand strategy · Messaging
03 Deliver
+

Whether launching or evolving a brand, this phase defines its structure and the tools for a clear, relevant and effective presence.For launches, refreshes or pivots, this is where the brand’s structure is defined, along with the tools to build a meaningful, clear and high-performing presence.

Naming · Visual identity · Design system
04 Implement
+

Here, the brand moves into execution. Campaigns, digital applications and internal channels are designed to express the identity consistently and without dilution.This is where the brand leaves the guidelines and enters real life. Campaigns, digital applications and internal channels are designed to carry the identity without dilution.

Campaigns · Digital applications · Editorial design

Brand systems are teamwork, and a system only proves itself in use, long after launch.Brand systems are teamwork. I work closely with strategists, copywriters, motion designers and developers, and I care about a system long after launch, because it only proves itself in use.
